chapters.title: Chapter 1: Numbers
chapters.description: Large numbers, Indian & International systems, place values, BIDMAS order of operations, and whole number properties.

concepts.title: Large Numbers & Number Systems
concepts.summary: Comparing Indian and International place value periods, reading numbers up to crores and billions.
key_points: Indian system periods: Ones, Thousands, Lakhs, Crores.
International system periods: Ones, Thousands, Millions, Billions.
1 Crore = 10 Million; 100 Lakhs = 1 Crore.

concepts.title: BIDMAS Rule & Order of Operations
concepts.summary: Mathematical expressions must be evaluated in the strict order: Brackets, Indices, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction.
key_points: B: Brackets first () [] {}
I: Indices or Powers
D & M: Division and Multiplication from left to right
A & S: Addition and Subtraction from left to right

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Introduction to Algebra
chapters.description: Patterns in shapes and numbers, algebraic variables, expressions, and solving unknowns.

concepts.title: Variables & Algebraic Expressions
concepts.summary: Using letters to represent unknown or changing values and translating word situations into algebraic statements.
key_points: A variable is an unknown value denoted by letters like x, y, n.
A constant has a fixed numerical value.
Algebraic expressions combine variables and constants using arithmetic operations.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Ratio and Proportion
chapters.description: Ratio comparison, simplest form, proportions, product of extremes and means, and unitary method.

concepts.title: Ratio, Proportion & Unitary Method
concepts.summary: Comparing quantities of the same unit through division and solving real-world rates using unit cost.
key_points: Ratio a:b compares two quantities of the same kind and unit; it has no unit.
In proportion a:b = c:d, Product of Extremes (a * d) equals Product of Means (b * c).
The unitary method finds the value of a single unit before calculating the total required.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Geometry
chapters.description: Lines, line segments, rays, parallel and perpendicular lines, angles classification, and collinear points.

concepts.title: Lines and Angles
concepts.summary: Fundamental geometric building blocks: points, lines, segments, rays, and angle classifications from acute to reflex.
key_points: A line extends infinitely in both directions; a line segment has two fixed end points.
Acute angle (< 90°), Right angle (90°), Obtuse angle (> 90° and < 180°), Straight angle (180°).
Parallel lines never intersect; perpendicular lines meet at 90 degrees.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Statistics
chapters.description: Data collection, tally marks, frequency distribution, pictographs, and bar graphs.

concepts.title: Data Representation & Bar Graphs
concepts.summary: Collecting raw numerical observations, organizing them using tally marks, and visualizing data with bar graphs and pictographs.
key_points: Tally marks group counts into bundles of five for easy tabulation.
Pictographs use pictures or symbols where each symbol represents a scaled quantity.
Bar graphs display categorical data using rectangular bars of uniform width.

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Information Processing
chapters.description: Systematic listing, tree diagrams, counting principles, and organizing combinations without omission.

concepts.title: Systematic Listing & Tree Diagrams
concepts.summary: Finding all possible outcomes or arrangements methodically using tree diagrams without missing any possibilities.
key_points: Systematic counting ensures every possible combination is counted exactly once.
Tree diagrams branch out to show multi-stage decision problems visually.
Fundamental counting principle simplifies large permutation calculations.
